title: A Microsoft 365 outage tied to Exchange Online knocks out email, Teams and Copilot for more than 12 hours
tldr: Microsoft 365 services that depend on Exchange Online failed worldwide from Thursday afternoon, and Microsoft's fixes had not brought sustained recovery more than 12 hours later.

title: Apache patches a critical HTTP/2 flaw in its web server that could let attackers run code remotely
tldr: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 fixes a critical race condition in its HTTP/2 module that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code on servers that have HTTP/2 switched on.

title: Police in nine countries seize 235 servers behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware
tldr: An Operation Endgame action coordinated by Europol took down 235 servers and 257 domains used by three malware families and found about 6.4 million stolen credentials.

title: Google opens pre-orders for its first Gemini smart glasses, made with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and Samsung
tldr: Google's camera-equipped "intelligent eyewear," starting at $395, is up for pre-order ahead of a December 10 launch, with privacy limits such as a tamper-checked recording light.

title: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays
tldr: A design for neutral-atom quantum computers that picks which qubits to operate on by moving helper atoms, letting simple global laser and microwave pulses run error-corrected computation in simulation.
byline: Zhihao Zhang, Shuaifan Cao, Xinyang Yu et al. · Fudan University

title: Attackers push rogue remote-access clients to hundreds of PCs through managed service providers' ScreenConnect panels
tldr: Attackers used cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to install rogue remote-access software on at least 288 computers at 48 organizations; ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions across about 400 partner environments.

title: Maersk confirms data theft from a legacy logistics system as a ransomware gang demands $5 million
tldr: Maersk says attackers stole data from an isolated system inherited through an acquisition; the WhiteArmor gang claims about 100GB and wants $5 million in bitcoin within 30 days.

title: The EU proposes a Digital Fairness Act to ban dark patterns, rein in addictive design and limit loot boxes for minors
tldr: The European Commission's draft Digital Fairness Act would ban manipulative "dark patterns," let users switch off addictive features, curb pay-to-win games for minors and allow fines of up to 6% of global turnover.

title: IBM's quantum roadmap swaps nine linked chips for two larger ones, targeting about 1,040 qubits in 2027
tldr: At its developer conference, IBM said its current Nighthawk r2 chip runs circuits of over 7,500 operations, and planned a 520-qubit Nighthawk r3 for 2027, with two chips linked into a roughly 1,040-qubit system.

title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
tldr: PRISM, a transformer-based decoder for photonic quantum computers, matches slower integer-programming decoders on accuracy and runs on an AMD FPGA with 6.59-microsecond latency.
byline: Daniel Barter, Jacob C. Bridgeman, Chris Dawson et al.

title: France formally blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for the cyberattacks that heated supermarket freezers
tldr: France says an Iranian Revolutionary Guards cyber unit sabotaged refrigeration controllers at more than 700 grocery stores, causing at least 15 fires, and plans to push for EU sanctions.

title: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday fixes over 1,000 flaws, including an Outlook bug already used to steal logins
tldr: Microsoft's monthly updates fix between 1,093 and 1,235 vulnerabilities depending on how they are counted, including an exploited Outlook spoofing flaw, alongside patches from Apple, Google, Mozilla and Adobe.

title: N-able takes its N-central remote-management cloud offline after a researcher publishes 30-plus unpatched flaws
tldr: After a researcher released working exploits for more than 30 alleged flaws without warning, N-able shut down hosted N-central worldwide and told on-premises customers to switch their servers off.

title: Mitsui Chemicals agrees to buy photoresist maker JSR for $11.6 billion
tldr: Mitsui Chemicals will pay 1.84 trillion yen for JSR, a leading maker of the light-sensitive coatings used to print chip circuits, in the largest deal ever in Japan's chemicals sector.

title: SFU-Sim: Bit-Exact Reverse Engineering of NVIDIA MUFU and Validation of PTX Paths
tldr: SFU-Sim reverse-engineers how Nvidia GPUs compute sine, cosine and other special functions, and its model matches real hardware bit for bit on every input across three GPU generations.
byline: Haozhi Xie, Tao Su · Sun Yat-sen University

title: Attackers are exploiting the "SSHole" OpenSSH flaw on Alpine-style Linux servers days after the fix
tldr: Several security firms report real attacks on the OpenSSH and musl flaw CVE-2026-123158, which can give logins to passwordless accounts; OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes it.

title: Vanderbilt University tells campus to shut down devices as the new BYOD ransomware gang claims an attack
tldr: Vanderbilt confirmed an active cyber incident and asked everyone to power off devices; a ransomware group called BYOD claims it stole data on over a million people.

title: Congress summons Nvidia's CEO over a reported Chinese spy operation, and Nvidia's board opens an investigation
tldr: House committee chairs asked Jensen Huang to brief them on November 18 about reported Chinese spying aimed at him; on Sunday Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation.

title: SonicWall patches a firewall VPN flaw that can sidestep SAML multi-factor login and is already exploited
tldr: SonicWall fixed seven SonicOS flaws, including CVE-2026-19868, which can bypass SAML-enforced MFA on SSL-VPN logins and was added to CISA's catalog of exploited bugs.
byline: SonicWall advisory (as quoted by SecurityWeek), BleepingComputer, Help Net Security

title: Chainalysis says hackers obtained credentials and live tokens for all of its users
tldr: Chainalysis, whose tools trace cryptocurrency flows, now says names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for every user were exposed, widening an incident first described as limited.

title: DigiCert says a 16-month exposure of an internal system let an outsider read customer identity documents
tldr: DigiCert says a server migration left an internal archive reachable from the internet from February 2025, and an unauthorized account read some customer records in June and July 2026.

title: Fox completes its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, five months after announcing it
tldr: Fox closed its $22 billion purchase of Roku, which reaches more than 100 million households, far earlier than the first-half-2027 completion the companies had projected.

title: AST SpaceMobile plans its own medium-lift rocket, backed by a $1.3 billion Firefly engine deal
tldr: The direct-to-phone satellite company says it will build Blacklift, a 20-ton-class rocket, and has committed $1.3 billion to Firefly for engines, a license and engineering support.

title: FaultScope: A software package for fast error attribution in quantum error correction
tldr: FaultScope is an open-source simulator that estimates how much each noisy component contributes to logical errors in quantum error correction, at under 1% extra runtime in tests.
byline: Yuguo Shao, Zhenyu Chen, Ningfeng Wang et al. · Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, Tsinghua University; Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications; Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

title: OpenSSH patch fixes "*sshole", a ten-year-old login bypass on musl-based Linux systems
tldr: OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes a flaw, present since 2016, that lets an oversized password log in to accounts meant to refuse passwords on musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine.

title: Blue Origin pushes the next New Glenn launch into January 2027 after May launchpad explosion
tldr: Blue Origin's CEO told staff the next New Glenn flight is now targeted for January 2027, after earlier hopes of launching before the end of this year.

title: FAA begins replacing floppy-disk-based air traffic displays with a digital system at more than 400 facilities
tldr: The FAA says it will replace 1980s display systems that run on floppy disks with the digital E-IDS platform, targeting 435 sites by the end of 2028.

title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware
tldr: Callix, a tool that judges whether access checks are strong enough for a sensitive operation, found 819 vulnerable paths in pre-installed apps from ten Android vendors.
byline: Haotian Deng, Meng Hao, Hanxiao Chen et al. · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

title: Second wave of attacks on refrigeration controllers hits supermarkets across Europe
tldr: Remote tampering with refrigeration controllers raised temperatures in more than 115 stores in six European countries on November 2, and also reached a French blood-service supplier, following a larger French wave in October.

title: Zyxel patches a switch flaw that was exploited on nearly 1,000 devices after being mistaken for an older bug
tldr: Zyxel fixed CVE-2026-107441 in ten GS1900 switch models after attackers used it to compromise 996 devices; the bug had been misattributed to an earlier, already-patched flaw.

title: Suspected Russian hackers use patched iPhone and Android flaws in watering-hole attacks
tldr: Sekoia says a group it links to Russia's foreign intelligence service used websites to profile visitors and attack phones that had not installed existing security updates.

title: DreamHost confirms a two-month breach of its File Manager exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
tldr: Web host DreamHost says an attacker exploited a flaw in its File Manager from August to October 23, stealing FTP/SFTP credentials and some webmail session data.

title: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal
tldr: Chip designer Marvell will acquire optical component maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt, expected to close in the first half of 2028.

title: Google and partners dismantle XCPE botnet built into 1.3 million Android TV boxes
tldr: Google's Threat Intelligence Group and partners disrupted XCPE, a backdoor that a Chinese manufacturer shipped in more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes to rent out owners' internet connections.
byline: Krebs on Security, Ars Technica, The Register

title: Binance says a fake job interview started its $6.3 billion theft
tldr: Binance's incident report says a multi-stage attack beginning with a fake recruiter and malware led to the October 29 theft of about $6.34 billion, which the FBI attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.

title: Apple warns memory costs are unprecedented as they squeeze margins and Mac supply
tldr: On its earnings call, Apple said memory pricing is unprecedented, forecast a December-quarter gross margin of 45 to 46 percent and expects Mac and iPad supply constraints.
